extracted.intended_audience: experimental/cognitive psychologists and researchers studying humor appreciation
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, running, and analyzing controlled experiments that test how priming, structural switches, and personality traits affect appreciation (funniness) and aversiveness of cartoons (humor structures NON vs INC-RES).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis 1 — Priming/salience (cognitive)
rubrics_metrics.description: If appreciation for humor structure may be enhanced by increasing the salience of structure through repeated exposure of a single structural type, then ratings of cartoons in the same prime ('stay') group should progressively increase. If appreciation is enhanced by the priming method, ratings of cartoons that precede a 'switch' in 'switch' groups should progressively increase before the switch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalize by creating 'stay' (control) groups with repeated presentation of one structure and measure funniness across trials to detect progressive increases; analyze within-subject priming effects across early trials (e.g., trials 1–3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis 2 — Switch salience and contrast effects
rubrics_metrics.description: If priming increases salience and salience influences preference, then the 'switch' cartoon in 'switch' groups should be rated significantly differently from cartoons preceding or following it. If the 'switch' cartoon is salient by contrast, then the 'switch/back' cartoon should be rated significantly differently from the 'switch' cartoon(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit 'switch' and 'switch/back' manipulations in sequence designs and test the serial-position effects of switches with planned comparisons (ANOVAs, t-tests) on the switch trial(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis 3 — Aversiveness priming effect
rubrics_metrics.description: If aversiveness ratings may be influenced by increasing the salience of structure through priming, then aversiveness ratings should decrease as a result of increased salience and increase as a result of interference when a 'switch' cartoon is introduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure aversiveness on the same numeric scale as funniness across trials; analyze aversiveness trial trends and interactions with prime and switch manipulations to evaluate predicted decreases/increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis 4 — Personality preference hypothesis (Sensation Seeking vs Conservatism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensation Seekers and Conservatives both find INC-RES funny, but only Sensation Seekers perceive NON as amusing. Sensation Seekers rate all humor as less aversive than Conservatives. Relative preferences: INC-RES less aversive for Conservatives; NON less aversive for Sensation Seekers. If personality determines structural preference independently of priming, funniness and aversiveness should vary according to structure and personality regardless of presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-select extreme personality groups and compare funniness/aversiveness across structures; analyze personality × structure interactions. Specific directional predictions: (A) high sensation seeking/low conservatism: funniness(NON) > funniness(INC-RES); opposite for low sensation seeking/high conservatism. (B) analogous directional predictions for aversiveness scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementary hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Appreciation for humor structure will depend upon an interaction between context (priming), structure (NON vs INC-RES), and personality (trait tolerance for ambiguity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test three-way interactions (prime × structure × personality) in multivariate analyses (MANOVAs) to evaluate whether personality moderates priming effects on structure appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor measurement — 3WD humor scale, funniness and aversiveness ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a validated humor scale (here: 3WD humor scale) with 14 cartoons (7 NON, 7 INC-RES). Each cartoon on a separate page with space for funniness and aversiveness ratings on scales from 0 (not at all funny/aversive) to 6 (very funny/aversive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect both funniness and aversiveness ratings for each stimulus; treat them as dependent variables in MANOVAs/ANOVAs; report means and SDs by trial and group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime/switch group design conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Create prime groups with defined sequences such as 'stay' (control: only one structure across trials), 'switch/switch back' (3 of A / 1 of B / 3 of A), 'switch/stay' (3 of A / 1 of B / 3 of B), and 'stay/switch' (3 of A / 1 of A / 3 of B), where A and B are NON and INC-RES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these structured serial presentations to operationalize priming and switch manipulations; ensure group sizes are approximately equal and representative; indicate which trial is the switch for planned comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus randomization and control for content effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Control for content effects by randomizing cartoon orders using Latin square technique so that across groups no cartoon occupies the same position in more than one grouping and no cartoon is followed by the same cartoon in more than one grouping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create multiple randomized orders (e.g., 32 orders) and repeat latin square orders for replication across first trials; use randomization to avoid confounding content with serial position or priming effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personality group selection thresholds (pre-selection criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form extreme personality groups using cutoffs: 'hiss/locon' (high Sensation Seeking/low Conservatism) — Sensation Seeking Boredom Susceptibility score ≥ 15 out of 20 and Conservatism score 3–18 out of 64; 'loss/hicon' (low Sensation Seeking/high Conservatism) — Sensation Seeking score 10 or 11 and Conservatism score 30–53.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preselect subjects based on these score ranges to create extreme groups for testing personality hypotheses; report n's and check whether personality is a significant factor in MANOVAs before interpreting interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random assignment and balancing procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign subjects randomly to prime context groups with the constraint of equally distributing subjects from personality categories across prime groups. Use master lists and session-wise randomization; adjust later sessions to even up short groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure approximately equal group sizes (n ~ 41–86 per subgroup as in the paper), and represent all prime context groups in each testing session to control session effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Test hypotheses using MANOVAs (e.g., 2 [prime structure] × 2 [personality] × 2 [switch 3→4] × 2 [switch 3→5] × 7 [trials]) and planned-comparison ANOVAs and t-tests for specific trial-level predictions. Use within- and between-subjects factors and report Pillai's approximate F when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include planned comparisons for the critical switch trials (4th and 5th), check main effects and interactions (prime × switch × score), and consider collapsing groups when nonsignificant treatment effects permit. Note conservative significance when using the original error term for collapsed comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical/procedural criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain informed consent (confidential no-deception consent form), inform subjects they may terminate participation at any time without penalty, and provide debriefing (explanation posted after participation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test subjects in small groups, record attendance/eligibility, and respect withdrawal rights; include debriefing after data collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus selection criterion for additional materials
rubrics_metrics.description: When adding stimuli (e.g., additional NON cartoons), select them based on prior experiment criteria (e.g., best predictors according to the personality preference hypothesis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use previous empirical results to choose supplementary stimuli to extend the design while maintaining construct validity (e.g., ensuring 7 INC-RES available and selecting 3 additional NON as best predictors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive rubric — salience vs dual-process vs habituation
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret differences in funniness/aversiveness in terms of competing theoretical accounts: 'salience hypothesis' (resolution salience drives appreciation), 'dual process' (sensitization then habituation), and 'context hypothesis' (sequence rules where appreciation higher when presentation establishes a structural link).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pattern of main effects and interactions across trials and switch manipulations to adjudicate among theories (e.g., priming increases appreciation supports salience/context; progressive increase then decrease supports dual-process).
